title: Keeping Watch on the Pressure

patient.name: Mr Chong Ah Beng
patient.presenting_complaint: Known glaucoma on eye drops — here for routine IOP monitoring

history.hpc: Mr Chong says 'I using the glaucoma drop, but sometimes I forget at night.' He is a known glaucoma patient on treatment, attending for routine IOP monitoring. He admits occasionally missing his evening drop.
history.pmhx: Primary open-angle glaucoma on a topical glaucoma drop. No drug allergies.

investigations.task: Measure IOP for glaucoma monitoring, note the slightly raised readings and the missed-drop history, and report both to the doctor
investigations.key_points: Compare to target/normal range; readings of 22/24 are above normal; the missed evening drops are relevant to control; report adherence and readings to the doctor

diagnosis: IOP monitoring for a known glaucoma patient shows readings slightly above normal (22/24 mmHg) in the context of occasionally missed evening drops. The OA records the readings, notes the adherence issue, and reports both to the doctor for review of control. No medical diagnosis is made by the OA.

immediate: Confirm identity and perform hand hygiene; wipe machine contact parts
Ask the patient to remove glasses or contact lenses
Explain the air puff and perform NCT right eye first
Record both readings in mmHg and note they are above the normal range
Ask about and note adherence to the glaucoma drops (missed doses)
Report the readings and the adherence issue to the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to review glaucoma control and reinforce adherence
Consider Goldmann tonometry if a more accurate reading is needed
patient_education: Reinforce taking the glaucoma drops regularly, including the evening dose
Explain that pressure control protects the optic nerve
